summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Quick Start Tutorial (2023 Updated Version) - Part 5: Create Panels in 2D Window In this tutorial video, we use the 11th version of Doshi Marvelous Designer. If you need to learn the 10th version of Marvelous Designer, please watch the previous video. In order to make it easier to learn, the Doshi Marvelous Designer is used in this tutorial. Now let's learn how to create a template in the 2D window. ## Importing a Virtual Model First of all, we need to import a virtual model. In this tutorial video, we will use Feifei from FemaleVR. 1. Stop your mouse on the multidirectional tool and select the rectangle tool from the drop-down menu. 2. Start from the center of the model, hold down the left mouse button, and drag the mouse to draw a rectangle according to the body shape of the virtual model, positioning it appropriately. 3. Change the texture display type to semi-transparent surface. Now you can adjust the template by using the virtual model screenshot. ## Adding Markers When the mouse is stuck on the tool, click on "Add Marker" on the lower left. 1. In the line in front, at the lowest position of the ruler and the highest position of the line, press the left mouse button separately to add 2 points. 2. Then, add 1 point at the bottom of the page. Ensure that there are some points below the bottom of the model screenshot, rather than just the one below the model screenshot. Next, select the tool of editing HTML. Once we have confirmed these points, we can delete the excess points. Adjust the point on the outside of the shoulder according to the angle of the shoulder line. Please note that this shoulder line should be as parallel to the model's shoulder as possible, which helps to create a more harmonious clothing pattern. ## Drawing Collar and Sleeve Curve Lines Next, let's draw the collar and sleeve curve lines. 1. In the drop-down menu, find the editor curve point tool, and click on the straight line to create a curve point. 2. Drag the curve point to adjust the corner of the collar and other panels as a straight line, ensuring it becomes a smooth curve when pasting other panels. 3. Use the same method to draw the sleeve curve, and also maintain the corner of the collar as a straight line. You can increase the curve point to adjust the details. The sleeve curve line should be shaped into a straight line, with the upper curve being flatter and the bottom curve more pronounced. Now we have completed one side of the front panel. ## Mirroring the Front Panel to Create the Back Panel Please select the adjustment panel tool. 1. On this panel, click with the right mouse button and select "Copy." 2. Click on the empty place in the background and select "Mirror Pasting." Next, we will modify this mirror pasting panel to create the back panel. In the previous tutorial of the 3D window of the creation panel, we mentioned that the collar of the back panel is a little lighter than the front panel. 1. First, use the editor curve tool to increase the center point of the back neck. 2. Then, adjust the shape of the back collar using the editor curve point tool. Due to the curvature of the person's back, the back curve should be flatter compared to the front panel, which needs to consider the impact of the chest. The sleeve curve of the back panel is also flatter compared to the front panel, with the curve of the bottom being shorter and larger. ## Creating the Sleeve Panel Next, let's learn how to create a sleeve panel. 1. Select the rectangle tool and draw a half-sleeved sleeve panel. Draw a rectangle that is wider than the arm; the length can be customized. 2. Use the adjustment panel tool to rotate it to a parallel position with the arm, aligning the highest point to the sharp point. 3. Select the plus point line tool and add a point near the bottom of the page. After completion, switch to the adjustment panel tool, right-click on the panel, select "Rotate X-axis," and click on the bottom to rotate the panel back. Now we can delete the excess points. ## Adjusting the Sleeve Panel Line Now we will use the editor curve tool to adjust the sleeve panel line. 1. Add curve points and adjust according to the effect in the video. The front sleeve panel line should typically run from top to bottom, first protruding and then arching, with the point in the middle position. 2. Use the edit panel tool, right-click on the middle line, and select "Open." The panel will open along this line. Please note that because the sleeve itself is not a symmetrical shape, we choose to open it instead of opening the editor in a symmetrical way. When modifying the sleeve panel line, we can move the front panel's curve points inwards a little to narrow down the width of the sleeve on this side. Conversely, for the back panel, we need to move the curve point of the protruding curve line outwards to widen the width of the sleeve on this side. The curve point from the protruding curve line to the arching curve line should be about one-third to one-fourth of the sleeve panel. ## Completing the Sleeve Panel Now a sleeve panel is completed. After we finish the curve line, we can adjust more details. 1. Choose the edit panel tool, right-click on each panel, and select the "Column Symmetrical Panel," panel, and curve line, then click OK. When a panel is in a symmetrical relationship, modifying one of the panels will also update the other panel symmetrically. When moving the symmetrical panel from the curve, press the Shift key to place the panel in the horizontal direction. Do the same for the back panel and the sleeve panel. ## Creating the Chest Pocket Next, let's make the chest pocket. 1. Select the mouse on the multidirectional tool, and then select the rectangle tool from the drop-down menu. 2. In the 3D window, click on the appropriate position, and use the blue reference point that appears simultaneously in the 2D window to draw the pocket line. The two front panels will also show the internal rectangle, as there is a symmetrical relationship between these two panels. These internal rectangles represent the seam positions of the pockets. 3. Next, we are going to remove the pocket panel. Select the mouse on the edit panel tool, then choose the pocket line from the drop-down menu. 4. In the frame selection, right-click on the internal rectangle and select the pocket panel. Please note that the pocket panel is not symmetrical but an independent panel. ## Saving the Project Now that we have completed the creation of the T-shirt panel, please save this project as a project file. In the follow-up tutorial, we will learn how to arrange and separate these panels to complete the costume. Thank you for watching! See you in the next video. ```
